free_tier.stated: No published total quota and no published per-file number that could be verified on 2026-10-21 - the author docs, the ideas board and the support KB were all behind SSO or Cloudflare. What IS verifiable is the observed size distribution: live file listings show modpacks at 89.1, 101.6 and 468.1 MB, and a single mod file at 66.7 MB. The one hard number surfaced is a *media* cap of 2 MB for images ('Why is it only 2MB??' - author complaint, still open, 'Future consideration'), and a forum report of a 350 MB mod upload being rejected without an external-URL option.
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.stated: No per-object cap documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
per_object_cap.notes: extraction found no per-object clause; some of these providers meter on object count rather than bytes, and some state no cap

retention.stated: retention: indefinite for approved files; 'Files updates in order to increase visibility is not allowed' and files must carry a changelog

egress.terms: Free and CDN'd via CloudFront in front of S3: edge.forgecdn.net and mediafilez.forgecdn.net return 'X-Cache: Miss from cloudfront' and 'Server: AmazonS3'. No billing. Hotlink-protected - a guessed object path returns 403 from S3 rather than bytes, so URLs must come from the API.

tooling: Official upload API with `X-API-TOKEN` and multipart `metadata` + `file` (third-party implementations exist, e.g. TeamDman/SuperFactoryManager and BreakBB/DisenchantBuddy shell out to it); `cfwidget` mirrors file metadata (id, filesize, uploaded_at) publicly. No SFTP, no rclone.
chaining: Unlimited projects per author account, unlimited files per project, unlimited versions. But every project and file enters a moderation queue ('your project is still awaiting moderator approval'), and the moderation policy explicitly forbids 'multiple similar and/or low effort projects in an attempt to game the system'. The provider therefore polices project count and not only request rate.

limits.value: review gate', not as bulk storage

limits_note: per-object-cap: unverified on 2026-10-21; evidence points below 500 MB for mods (350 MB rejection reported, 468.1 MB modpack published, so the ceiling is game-dependent and enforced client-side per the August release notes: 'Added new client-side validation - preventing upload of large files on unsupported games'). retention: indefinite for approved files; 'Files updates in order to increase visibility is not allowed' and files must carry a changelog. request-rate: not published.

identity_cost.detail: no identity_cost field and no identity statement in the source record; defaulted to email and flagged, not evidence

reliability_note: Reads are hotlink-gated (403 from S3 on constructed URLs) and the whole author surface is SSO-walled, so this is the least auditable of the game hosts. Moderation is active and rule-driven. Best treated as 'large-ish files with a review gate', not as bulk storage.

extras.agent_focus: The code-forge seam: OSS project hosts, software-download directories, game/mod distribution and mirror services. Question for each: (a) any published byte quota, (b) is upload possible over SFTP/rsync/SCP/SSH rather than a web form, (c) is there a public download CDN, (d) does it need an approved project or can any account create one, (e) per-file cap. Round 2 flagged that SourceForge has no published quota and serves over plain SFTP with a global mirror CDN, and that an rclone-backend enumerator would score the niche as empty. This slot tests that class systematically. Every number below was read live or from a dated archive capture on 2026-10-21.

binding_note: the write is a queue with a person or a rule in it, so the upload rate is set by somebody else
